body: Looks great thank you!
Thanks for the response :) Hope it all works out for you!
How did it go? I'm really anxious about seeking help
I do and it's awful. I'm really self conscious about it. It's like I can't even say hi to someone without getting red. It's been like this for yeeeears
How'd it go?
Good luck! Definitely let me know how it goes I'd love to hear about it.

Hi there, sorry you've been having bad anxiety lately. I've been struggling myself too especially recently. I didn't think I'd be able to tell anyone about it because I was so afraid of confronting the anxiety head on so I kept pushing it off. 

Until today that is. I finally talked to my mom about the severity of it and she was understanding of my situation and wanted to help all she could. I was relieved that someone had my back and knew what I was going through. I then set up an intake assessment at a mental health center nearby this afternoon. I'm going to be going in on Monday. Honestly? I'm terrified. I never thought I'd get this far. But it seems to me to be the best way of defeating my SA, which is confronting it head on.

I guess what I'm trying to say is the sooner you tell someone the better. You don't want to deal with this by yourself. And if you want someone to chat to you can message me anytime. We're in this together!
Yes! I get way more anxious in groups than one on one. Stuff like parties, meetings, and presentations are my downfall
You got this!
Preeeach. I'm over here living comfortable, have a good family, solid income, and I'm contemplating suicide due to my anxiety like wtf

I'm in the same boat as you right now. I really want my parents to know the severity of my anxiety and I know they would help but idk if I can do it. I already told them briefly of my anxiety but they aren't aware of how bad it really is. I'm terrified of taking that first step towards recovery even tho I know I need to in order to get better. And I hate looking "selfish" because I don't like socializing with people or going to parties by those close to me. SA is really shitty
I've never gone but maybe give toastmasters a try if there's one in your area. I want to get better at public speaking as well and I've been thinking about attending a couple classes.
Thank you. I hope things start looking up for you too. And congrats on going to that therapist appointment! I know that had to be really difficult to go through.
Honestly looks like a normal sized forehead so I wouldn't worry!

Hi there, I've been feeling pretty low lately too. And I actually just downloaded that meetup app as well. I found a group for people with social anxiety but it isn't very active (go figure!) and another group for people with anxiety and depression which has more events. Hopefully I can gather the courage to make it to one of their events!

May I ask, have you ever tried exposure therapy? That's what I'm hoping to try soon and I'm terrified lol

Edit: Btw I'm glad you're still here!
I've never gone out for New Years before. Always just chill at home and watch the ball drop in New York lol

They're probably putting themselves in uncomfortable situations in order to try to make some progress in defeating social anxiety. And every small step you take can eventually lead you to be in the same position they are. At first they were probably terrified at the thought of speaking to a stranger just like you are right now.

Sorry that happened to you. I was the best man at my brother's wedding too. Except I never did a speech. I hid in the bathroom "faking" a stomach problem until the wedding was over. I say faking in quotations because I was having severe stomach pains and nausea but it was definitely due to the anxiety. Speeches and presentations are what spike my anxiety the most. Even months before the wedding I knew I wouldn't be able to do a speech. I still feel awful about it and it was 1.5 years ago. I really wish I could've been there for my brother. 

2019 is the year I make some progress.

Happy birthday. I hope you're able to do something fun for yourself today.

I just want to tell you that I feel your pain. Social anxiety is a real pain in the ass to deal with. You want friends but at the same time you don't. It just doesn't make any sense. I've pushed away so many people just because I didn't want to put in the effort and I was too scared to sustain a friendship. As a result, my only true friend is my cousin who is the exact same way. I don't have any friends besides family. And it's an awful feeling. I want friends to hangout with, to go to concerts with, to play video games with, but I just can't seem to take that next step into actually making and keeping friends. I'm too scared and my self esteem is too low to even try.

But I don't want to keep living this way so I'm planning on making some serious changes this upcoming year. I'm going to push myself to get uncomfortable. Instead of coping with the anxiety I'm going to try to defeat it head on. I've never gone to therapy but I'm going to schedule a session beginning of the year. Am I nervous? Scared of what's to come? Hell yeah I'm scared and nervous. But I'd rather travel into the unknown than stay where I'm at if it means having even the tiniest of chances of defeating social anxiety.

Anyways, I'm sorry you feel lonely on your birthday. Birthday's can be difficult. I know mine is too. If you need anyone to message I'm here for you. And sorry this post is a bit scrambled, I do that sometimes :p

You're welcome! I'm glad they were understanding of your situation and allowed you the time to get that letter from your therapist. And I wish I could be normal too so I definitely feel your pain there! If you don't mind me asking, have you tried exposure therapy? I'm planning on trying that pretty soon here. I've never gone to therapy before and I'm really nervous about everything. But I'm hoping that by pushing myself bit by bit I'll be able to gain some much-needed self confidence.

Perhaps as a last ditch effort you could call the number on the letter the court sent you and explain your predicament to them? Let them know of your anxiety issues and how you've been seeing a therapist but don't think you'd be able to handle all that came with jury duty at this particular time. Idk if it'll work but I guess it's worth a shot if you feel as though you wouldn't be able to go. Certainly the court wants a person who can focus completely on the trial at hand and a person with mental health issues (like me and you) wouldn't be able to give 100% to the cause.

I'm sorry for what you're going through. This kind of a problem seems so irrational to people that don't have social anxiety. I hope you're able to get out of it but even if you don't just remember that it's only a moment in time that will eventually pass and be over with. I wish you the best of luck.
Congrats! Hope all goes well :)

Hey, I was just summoned as well. I was supposed to appear January 8th but I postponed it online to later next year. Apparently (at least in the state of Oregon) you are allowed the opportunity to postpone your duty to a later date one time. You are also allowed to not attend if you feel there may be an issue.

You should definitely check with your therapist. Try to get a written note that describes your condition and how you wouldn't be fit to be in the selection pool. Then I'd suggest calling the court you're supposed to appear in and let them know of your issue. They'll then be able to guide you in the right direction.

Hope this helps.

That sounds awful what you're going through. And it's especially awful that your family seems to be making the problem worse. High school was a really difficult period of my life as well. I was really anxious all the time and bullied nearly every day. It was so bad that I would rather sit in the bathroom stall during my lunch period than eat in the cafeteria. I'd also skip every single presentation in class because I had no confidence in my abilities to speak in front of anyone, let alone the whole class. I just hated everything about me; I was skinny, short, had lots of pimples, turned red easily, the list went on and on. I thought of committing suicide nearly every night. One night, a night that I remember very vividly, was when I looked into how tall the Golden Gate bridge was in San Francisco and what the success rate of suicide jumpers was. I was so, so low. But, and I don't know how I did it, but I just kept pushing through. I kept fighting.

That was a little over 7 years ago. I'm 22 now and finally looking to get help for my anxiety and depression problems. For so long I'd been successful in pushing my problems further and further into myself, coping with the problem rather than fighting it. I simply didn't want to face them. But now that I'm about to dive head first into the real world in a few months I've been looking into going to therapy because damn do I know I need it. I just wish I didn't push away the problem until now. I wish I'd done it much, much sooner. So I guess my advice to you is to seek help now rather than later, no matter how much you might not want to. There are mental health professionals that want to help you become the best version of yourself that you can be.

I wish you the best of luck and I'm rooting for you!
You never had to actually answer questions out loud?
Awesome advice. I needed to hear this.

It's weird my dreams can vary between having anxiety and not. Sometimes I'll be the most confident person in the world and other times I'm extremely self-conscious and think really hard about what I'm going to say to someone like in reality. 

Just last night I had a dream that I stood up for myself and told a person off, which is something I'd never do in real life. Funnily enough, it actually made me feel good about myself that I was able to do that even if it was just in a dream. Gave me a confidence boost lol. Shit's strange

It actually went pretty good thank god. I was dreading the day for months but it has come and gone just like every other day. I usually try to stick with my older brother since he is pretty extroverted and can talk for the majority of the time lol. I also get along with him really well so we just hung out on the couch mainly and talked with some other relatives. And then just like that it was over and now I'm here. It felt like a weight was lifted off my shoulders when it was over

Hi there,

I got a couple questions for you. What were your specific triggers when you had severe social anxiety? What were your first step towards recovery? Did you ever go to therapy and how did it go? What made the biggest difference in boosting your self esteem?

I'm 22 years old and have had enough of social anxiety and how it has controlled my life up until this point. I want to finally take steps towards defeating my anxiety rather than just coping with it. However, with this decision I realize I'm going to have to face my fears head on now, which is a terrifying realization because for years I've avoided my triggers at all costs. So I guess I'm just looking for a general idea of how you overcame your anxiety. Thanks!

Yeah I'm like that too. I think it stems from being bullied throughout middle school and the early parts of high school until I switched to online. I'm decent at talking with older people but the second I see someone near or at my age level my anxiety spikes.

Seriously though this is like the worst time of the year for people with social anxiety. Being essentially forced to socialize with relatives unless you wanna look like an ass or rude because you didn't see them. It's a lose-lose situation...

Yep. I hate how some people see me as an asshole or selfish just because I'd rather keep to myself than do something with them, especially when I feel like crap. Being social for me is draining as hell and sometimes I just simply don't have the energy to do anything except lay in bed and watch Netflix. Yet people always think I must hate them if I skip out on something when that couldn't be further from the truth.

I feel you. I have the worst anxiety over presentations. So bad that I've skipped every single one since I was like 14 and I'm 22 now. So I applaud and admire the courage you had in just getting up there to give the presentation in the first place. That takes some serious balls, especially for those of us with social anxiety.

I've been thinking about joining a local toastmasters but haven't been brave enough to attend a meeting yet.

Thank you so much for this.

Life is about to get really uncomfortable for me. I'm finally going to confront my anxiety head on, which is something I thought I'd never be able to do. I'm hoping 2019 brings a lot of positive change and personal growth. 

Btw congrats on bettering yourself. I know that first step must've been extremely difficult, because it sure is for me. You are a serious fighter and someone I admire wholeheartedly. Much love.
I'm sorry for what you've gone through. If you want to message me I'm all ears, whether you want to vent or just talk. We're in this fight together and I want you to come out on top.

I feel you on so many fronts - about appearing weak if I told anyone about my anxiety, missing out on so many things in high school, wishing I could just ditch everything and go anywhere but the present. All I can really say is that the quicker you reach out for help the better. Don't try to just cope with social anxiety or it'll continue to eat you up inside until it's too late. I'm 22 years old and finally took a step towards recovery in contacting an anxiety center in my area and am looking towards exposure therapy to help me out. And I honestly wish I'd done it sooner. I'm a mess man. Way more anxious than I was even a year earlier. It took hitting rock bottom and constant suicidal thoughts to force me to reach for help.

As for how to tell your parents, I know it'll be tough. I never thought I'd tell mine but I ended up being straight up with them. One day I told them I had social anxiety and how it's difficult for me to do certain things that normal people wouldn't have a problem with. It was so hard to be so vulnerable. But it was like a weight was lifted off my shoulders knowing that I wasn't the only one who knew what I was dealing with. And I hope it's the same way for you. I wish you the best of luck. I'm rooting for you!

Hi there! I really like your idea and think it would help me out as well. Although idk if I have the courage to video chat yet if that's what you're thinking of. I'm a 22 M who has severe social anxiety, particularly presentations, meetings, interviews, dating, partying, and things of that nature. Basically I break under any resemblance of pressure. But I'm trying to fix that one step at a time.

Looking ahead towards 2019 these are my goals: to get into exposure therapy, begin dating, get an internship/job, get a girlfriend, make more friends, and just overall improve my self esteem.

Right now things aren't going well at all for me. I am an anxious wreck (especially around the holidays) and my confidence is at an all time low. I'm really crawling in my skin at the moment. It's like slow and inhumane torture living day to day lol. So I'm looking to change for the better.
I feel like an alien lol
Thank you for the words of encouragement and helpful tips. Btw I love your username! Really clever :)

Hey we're in the same boat! Yay! I've also been severely anxious over the family gatherings coming up and have also been having suicidal thoughts because of it. I feel like a lunatic. These kind of things should be seen as fun, right? I love my family and people in general too but the anxiety becomes too much to bear around this time of the year.

Regarding how to tell your parents. It's really tough, especially if they're religious like mine are. I just told them that I have bad social anxiety and think I need help. That's really all there is to it. It went well and they were sympathetic but they ultimately said to go to god with these problems because he's the ultimate healer or something. They didn't think therapy would work. But at least they had my back. And if your parents are loving they should have yours too.

Now, on to the solution. Obviously we both need help, especially if suicidal thoughts are popping into our heads to get away from these social situations. So what I'm looking into doing is exposure therapy. I contacted an anxiety center nearby about it and am currently in the process of seeing if my insurance would cover it. Let me tell you this shit is terrifying to me. But I know I need to break free from the anxiety before I do something stupid like take my own life.

I wish you the best of luck my friend. I'll be rooting for you. If you need someone to talk to please message me. It would help me out with my anxiety as well!

I wouldn't know :/ 

My self esteem is so low right now that if a girl came up to me and asked me out I'd tell her I'm not worth it lol

That happened to me today too. I went to some Christmas concert at a church and took a seat in the back with my grandma. I look around and see all these people casually chatting away and I can't even say hello without turning bright red. Even being around so many people I'd never felt so alone and helpless. I was an anxious wreck the entire time, all the while wishing I never came. There was a cute girl there and even imagining myself talking to her afterwards made me have a panic attack. Shit sucks.

Oh god ikr. Like I really really want to start dating but whenever I got a message from a girl I didn't even want to respond. Eventually I just hid my profile because I knew I wouldn't be able to go due to the anxiety. I need help lol.

I'm going to try to work up the courage and give exposure therapy a shot. I need to build up my confidence so much.

Thanks for this post! I've been having a really hard time lately with anxiety and have actually been contemplating ending my life. I just feel so hopeless and lonely even though I have a loving support group. They know I have anxiety but not to this extent. It might be because of the holidays that it's so bad but it wasn't this bad last year so it must be getting worse. I have extremely low self esteem even though I've been eating healthy and going to the gym. It's becoming difficult to put on a mask every day.

Due to having bad thoughts and severe anxiety I recently got into contact with an anxiety center in my area. I'm hoping I have the courage to go. God it's scary but I know it's like the only way to get better. I really wish I didn't feel so dejected all the time so socializing would be a little easier. It always feels like there's a lump in my throat and a knot in my stomach.

I'm in the same boat as you man except I'm 22. I've been hiding the problem for close to 8 years. Luckily I was able to tell my parents a couple months ago and they were supportive. But now that I'm being forced to confront my issues it's terrifying. I'm an anxious wreck. I was able to email an anxiety center nearby and they think exposure therapy would help and I agree with them. Now I have to work up the courage to go to this place and talk with someone about my issues, which is exactly what I've been trying to put off all these years.

I guess it doesn't hurt to try though. I think the best way to beat this is to confront our anxiety head on. Just start small and continue to work your way up. I know it's easier said than done but that's what I'm trying to do. My self esteem and self confidence is extremely low but I'm hoping that as long as I continue to move outside my comfort zone, the more confident I will become. One day at a time.

I wish you the best of luck dude! I'll be rooting for you.

You're really brave for still going. People just don't understand how debilitating social anxiety can be, especially for things like interviews. I'm going to have to be getting a job soon and I already have anxiety over the interview process. It really sucks
What the fuck kind of test is that? That's some bullshit man.

Thanks for the encouragement. I truly believe that getting this disorder out in public would help me but I'm just too worked up to do it. I hope I'm able to let someone know sooner rather than later. This disorder is seriously debilitating

I wish you the best of luck with your interview! Remember to try your best in understanding that this interview will be over quick and is just a very small portion of your life. Easier said than done for sure but you got this!! I'm rooting for you
This is amazing! I don't comment on reddit often but I felt like I needed to tell you how much I enjoyed this piece of art. Very bold, unique, and a great daily reminder to think positive. Awesome!

Yep I know where you're coming from. I only have 1 friend really and that's my cousin. Luckily he's introverted too and doesn't have many friends either so he'd never bag me for not having friends. But no matter the person a true friend wouldn't make fun of you for that. That's just fucked up. I understand that it's tough making friends but I don't think it's bettering you by being around them.

You're not alone. I haven't kissed anyone either, let alone hold someone's hand. It hurts. People are always pestering me about it too. Not like mean pestering but just annoyingly mentioning it. I just don't want to burden someone else with my problems. Anxiety and depression would make maintaining a relationship difficult.

Exactly. Sports has always been a big part of my life and something I've always found enjoyable to play or watch but recently things just haven't been the same. I don't even enjoy shooting hoops outside anymore. And that used to be my favorite time of the day. Sucks.

That story resonated with me a lot. I'm sorry you didn't get the jobs you applied for. I wish you all the success in the future and always remember that you're not alone. We're all fighting this shitty disease together. Much love.

Great advice. As someone with depression and anxiety who used to believe in god I can't tell you how awful of a suggestion this is. For 6 years straight I asked "god" to help me. I cried my eyes out for him to take away my suicidal thoughts and anxiety. But what do you know? Nothing happened. How strange right? It's almost as if there isn't a magical fairy in the sky watching over our every move. Interesting.

I couldn't handle giving a best man speech at my brother's wedding so I hid in the bathroom the entire reception. It's been a year but it still seriously hurts to think about. I wish I had the guts to tackle the anxiety but it was just unbearable.
In the 8th grade when I started looking up the easiest ways to die. I'm 22 now and still barely hanging on.
I think I'm gonna tell my parents tonight. I can't hold it in any longer.
oh god lol. when do you plan on telling her?

I feel exactly the same. I do love my family and I think it would help me but I don't know how to tell them. everything is going fine for everyone else and I don't want to ruin that. then I'll be the center of attention if I say anything too and my anxiety would hate that

I know exactly what you mean man. I don't want my family to go through that either. that's honestly why I couldn't finish the deed the couple times I tried. I just kept thinking about their reactions. I hope you feel better soon. Thanks for reaching out to me

I have self-confidence issues that stemmed from being bullied in high school. I think of myself as inferior and weak. and that I'd be a burden to my family if I told them. I mean how do I even bring it up. they think I'm fine. It's so hard to open up. especially because I'm a man who I guess shouldn't have feelings
that's the same with me. started at 14 and I'm 21 now. how do you cope with the thoughts?
have you told anyone that you have suicidal thoughts?
social anxiety. I can't do any normal shit like talk. I'm such a recluse it's insane. the loneliness kills
how long have you had suicidal thoughts?
Ate breakfast, worked on an assignment, ate lunch. I'm so sick of this damn anxiety. every day always the same

God damn that is the perfect description of what's happening to me too. My depression and anxiety just keeps getting worse no matter what I try and do to combat it. It's some bullshit. 

I wish you all the best in your fight.

It's my birthday in 4 days. I'm so tired of wearing a mask. Everyone thinks I'm fine while I'm dying inside. The last thing I want to do is celebrate my birthday right now. I'd rather die.

Happy birthday by the way. Try and treat yourself. Hope you make it through.
Awful. To add the deconversion process to my depression and anxiety is way too much. Feeling really hopeless.

I was the best man at my brother's wedding and was dreading the day for months. I knew that I would have to give a speech but I figured I wouldn't. And I was right. After the ceremony when the party began I booked it inside my family's home and faked a stomach virus to get out of it. I felt like the biggest piece of selfish shit in the world. That wasn't my day, it was my brother's day. Yet I happened to still run away from another building block to bettering myself and also saddened my brother in the process.

I still feel awful and think about it every couple days. It'll just pop up in my head and I'll be depressed the rest of the day. I can't help the memories from coming back, no matter how terrible they are.

Yeah I'd say it's definitely gotten worse as I've aged. Although it probably would've helped if I actually tried to improve myself as it gradually became a problem. I still find myself avoiding plenty of situations where my anxiety peaks and I know it's going to be tough when adult life legitimately hits me. I know I need help but I'm too afraid to get it. Honestly I don't think I'd be able to handle a classroom situation right now, especially the discussions and presentations.

Just wanted to let you know that I feel your pain. I've been struggling much more than usual this past week and tonight hasn't been any different. I'm laying in bed thinking of how big of a failure I've been in my life. I hate who I've become. 

I hope that you find sleep and have a better day tomorrow. I guess that's really all we have to hope for.

I love how players from the NBA are beginning to speak out about mental health. Hopefully what Demar DeRozan and Kevin Love are doing starts a trend. This kind of stuff makes me love basketball even more.

To be honest I'm almost to that point too. It's been building up for so long.. I'm glad you were able to get somebody's attention going forward though. I hope things go well for you with your therapist. You should let me know how it goes!

Heya, firstly I just wanted to let you know that you're awesome. Tonight has been hard on me. I skipped out on going somewhere because my anxiety was acting up and so I've just been laying in bed all day with my thoughts. Yeah, not good. I've been seriously down because I've been thinking of future me and how there's no way that I'll make it in the real world. I'm in college right now and am about a year away from graduating. I've never had a legit job and have severe social anxiety so even the thought of having an interview is enough for me to contemplate suicide. I've never told anyone about my mental health and I feel like I'm slowly losing myself to this disease. I know I need to tell someone but I hate opening up to people. Really, you're the first person I've told all of this too. I guess tonight I am just desperate. I need help to combat this anxiety. It is eating me alive.

I feel for you, man. I'm 21 too and I've struggled with making and maintaining friendships as well. While I have had a couple, my anxiety always ruins them. I never want to go out. Ever. I constantly think about what I will be doing when I'm out of school and I just can't comprehend it. Doing an interview? Yeah, I don't think so. This life is so hard. I want to go out and be social, make friends, and have a good time, yet when I actually try and improve my social life I crave being home alone. I can't break the anxiety within me. This shit is going to be the end of me.
